citation: herdr src/session.rs and src/config/io.rs, at the v0.8.0 tag
why: Where a daemon listens is reimplemented from herdr's own rules rather than asked for, which makes it exactly the kind of thing that drifts silently. Getting it wrong does not crash Muster: it falls back to guessed encodings, and arrow keys stop working in pagers while everything else looks fine. Precedence is HERDR_SOCKET_PATH, then a named HERDR_SESSION, then the default session's socket, with the base directory from XDG_CONFIG_HOME or HOME.

cases.name: an explicit socket path beats everything else
cases.why: First in precedence, and set by anyone pointing Muster at a daemon that is not where the rules would put it. Every other variable here is populated too, so a rule applied in the wrong order would be visible.

cases.name: an empty explicit path is ignored rather than obeyed
cases.why: An exported-but-empty variable is a normal state of a shell profile. Treating it as a real answer would produce a connection attempt against the empty path instead of falling through to the rules.

cases.name: a named session gets its own socket
cases.why: herdr puts non-default sessions under sessions/<name>/, so a client that ignored HERDR_SESSION would find the default daemon and mirror the wrong session entirely.

cases.name: the default session is spelled by absence, not by name
cases.why: HERDR_SESSION=default must not produce a sessions/default directory, because no daemon listens there. The name is a synonym for the base path.

cases.name: an empty session name is the default session
cases.why: Same reasoning as the literal `default`, reached by the more common route of an exported-but-unset variable.

cases.name: XDG_CONFIG_HOME moves the base directory
cases.why: The isolated daemon the contract tier spawns works exactly this way. Getting it wrong would make that whole tier connect to the developer's own daemon, or to nothing, while still reporting a pass.

cases.name: nowhere to look is nothing, not a guess
cases.why: Returning a plausible-looking path would turn `there is no daemon here` into a connection error somewhere further from the cause, which is the kind of misdirection that costs an afternoon.

cases.name: an empty HOME is nowhere to look
cases.why: The same as no HOME at all. A path built from an empty base would be rooted at /.config/herdr, which is not a mistake worth making silently.
